p: Here's a bit of Leeds history to chew on between frames: Marks and Spencer began life as a penny bazaar stall in Leeds Kirkgate Market back in 1884. The market is still going strong today, just a short walk from Boar Lane, and it's one of the best places in the city to grab a cheap bite or browse a huge variety of stalls. It's a great warm-up before a night on the lanes.

A few tips for your visit. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. Book ahead for Friday and Saturday nights, and think about how many lanes you'll need. Four to six people per lane is about right, so bigger groups should consider two. Swapping teams around halfway through keeps things fair and stops one player running away with it.

If you're arriving early and fancy something to do, Leeds Minster, near the river, is a beautiful church with a long history. Further down by the water, the Royal Armouries Museum at Leeds Dock houses the national collection of arms and armour, with displays ranging from medieval jousting to modern-day warfare. It makes a fascinating afternoon.

Getting home is easy too. Leeds station is just a few minutes away, so you can bowl until your last train and still make it with time to spare. Just keep an eye on the clock once the competition heats up.
